title: Learning From the Shadow
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece makes the case for formal shadowing as an underused but highly effective onboarding and development tool. The author describes an ideal shadowing arrangement as lasting only a few days, with the observer taking notes quietly and the expert narrating their thinking out loud as they work. A useful side effect noted in the piece is that explaining one's own process out loud often gives the expert new clarity about their own instincts. The piece singles out watching how experts handle messages and everyday exchanges as one of the most instructive things a shadow can observe. It closes with a quote from novelist Carlos Ruiz Zafon and a call for more organizations to formalize the practice.
points: Shadowing an expert accelerates learning more effectively than almost any other development method.
Ideal shadowing lasts just a few days, with the observer quiet and the expert narrating their thinking.
Explaining their own process out loud often gives experts new clarity about their own instincts.
Watching how experts handle everyday messages and exchanges is especially instructive for the observer.
quotes: Following the footsteps of those who have mastered the kind of performance or role we desire to play shows us what moves to make and what actions to avoid.
Yet, too few organizations formalize shadowing, even for new team members or those preparing to take on an unfamiliar role.
The person who is shadowing is a silent partner in observation, taking notes and asking questions only when the expert has a moment to give attention to the query.
They quickly learn that explaining what they do and how they do things often creates a new clarity in their own thinking.

Of the many ways we can gain insight, learn how things work, and come to appreciate the details connected to high performance, perhaps none is more powerful than to follow or shadow someone with experience and skill.
When coupled with feedback and review, shadowing an expert jumpstarts learning and socializes less experienced colleagues more quickly than just about anything else.
While some experts might view having another person tagging along as an unnecessary nuisance, the benefits clearly outweigh the inconvenience.
Watching the kind of information, challenges, and issues that confront an expert in real time gives the less experienced a crash course in how things get done with excellence.
